question.text: 'Asha Deep Trust' is a women-empowerment NPO registered as a public charitable trust in Maharashtra. Which legislation primarily governs its constitution and which document is its charter?

answer.text: Societies Registration Act 1860; the charter is the MOA and rules
FCRA 2010; the charter is the FCRA registration certificate
Companies Act 2013 Section 8; the charter is the MOA and AOA
Indian Trusts Act 1882 (for private trusts) / state public trust law in Maharashtra; the charter is the Trust Deed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (p.18), private trusts are governed by the Indian Trusts Act 1882, while public trusts in most states are governed by general law — except in states such as Maharashtra and Gujarat that have their own public trust laws. The constitutional document of a trust is the Trust Deed. The Trap: Option A applies to Societies. Option C applies to Section 8 Companies. Option B is FCRA — a foreign contribution registration, not the constituting law. Note: The legal-form comparison (Trust vs Society vs Section 8 Company) and the Trust Deed as the charter are directly supported by p.18 of the workbook.
